title: How to Actually Vet a Breeder Listing
body:
A friend mentions a breeder nearby, or a listing turns up close to home, and the obvious question is how you actually know it's a good one. Daily Paws recently rounded up the signs experts look for in a responsible breeder, and most of them come down to something simple: does this person actually know and care for the animals they're placing, or are they just moving them along.

The signs are worth internalizing rather than treated as a checklist. A breeder who's proud of their work will usually let you see where the puppies or kittens actually live, not just a photo sent over WhatsApp. They'll answer questions about the parents' health and temperament without getting defensive, and they won't rush you toward a decision before you've had a chance to meet the animal in person. A breeder who avoids all of that, or pushes hard for a deposit before you've seen anything, is telling you more than any wording in a listing ever could.

That last part matters because a listing by itself can't tell you much. On PetMatch, like on most free directories, listings are self-reported by the person who posted them. Nobody at PetMatch is independently checking a breeder's registration, a vaccination card, or how the animals are actually kept. That's not a flaw unique to PetMatch; it's true almost anywhere people connect directly rather than through a shop. The difference is knowing that going in, so the actual vetting happens where it should, in person, before anything is agreed.

In practice that means talking on WhatsApp first, asking to see health and vaccination records rather than taking someone's word for them, and meeting somewhere you're both comfortable, a neutral spot or a partner vet clinic, before either side commits to anything. None of this makes finding a well-bred puppy or kitten harder. It just puts the judgment where it belongs, with the person actually meeting the breeder and the animal, not with whatever a listing happens to say.

More on meeting another owner safely is at https://petmatch.fit/safety.
